newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer, but avoid Dow sell off.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer, but avoid Dow sell off.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday, but media and energy stocks helped the Canadian market avoid New York's steep decline.
The TSE 300 Composite Index dropped 16.89 points to close at 5929.98 in brisk turnover of 112.6 million shares worth C$1.93 billion ($1.5 billion).
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average sank 51 points to close around 6549.
Despite weakness in golds, merchandising and transportation, "there was fair amount of strength in the (Toronto) market," said Jim Doak, director of investment research for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
The gold sector dropped 267 points as Comex February gold closed down US$2.90 an ounce at US$356.80 after hitting lows around US$355.30 an ounce.
The transport and merchandising groups also lost ground due to declines in individual stocks. The strong side was led by communications, oil and gas, and real estate.
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 500 to 486 with 257 issues unchanged.
* Loewen Group Inc. sank after rival Service Corp. International dropped its US$2.9 billion takeover bid.
Loewen dropped 5.95 to 49.75 on 3.8 million shares and depressed the TSE's merchandising group. The stock had hit a high of 58.75 during Loewen's takeover fight with Service Corp.
* Among weak golds, Barrick Gold Corp. fell 1 to 35.55, while Placer Dome Inc. slipped 0.55 to 27.05.

* Laidlaw Inc. class B dropped 0.60 to 17.40 on 4.3 million shares after soaring to new heights on Tuesday. Investors rushed to buy Laidlaw's stock after the company announced two major deals worth over US$2 billion late Monday.
* The top gaining energy stock was Dreco Energy Services Ltd. class A which closed up 2.25 to 53.75.
Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. added 0.40 to close at 10.70 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 10.75. Gulf Canada is currently in the midst of a takeover bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc.
